title: Whole Grain Pasta with Cream Sauce and Poultry

content.title: About
content.content: Whole grain pasta prepared at home with a smooth cream sauce and pieces of poultry combines the nutritional benefits of whole grains with the high‑quality protein of chicken. This dish is suitable for those seeking a balanced meal rich in fiber and vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole grain pasta retains the bran and germ, making it more nutritious than refined white pasta.
Cream sauce is often made from cream and a small amount of flour, giving the dish a velvety texture without excessive greasiness.
Poultry, especially chicken, is a lean source of protein packed with B‑vitamins.
A homemade recipe allows control over salt levels and the addition of aromatic herbs such as basil or oregano.
Whole grain pasta typically requires a slightly longer cooking time to achieve an al dente texture.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Whole grain pasta provides both soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting healthy digestion and stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Chicken delivers complete protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dish contains thiamine, niacin, and vitamin B6, which aid energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Beneficial fats
items.content: Cream, used in moderation, supplies saturated and monounsaturated fats along with fat‑soluble vitamins A and D.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Whole grain pasta and chicken provide iron, magnesium, and zinc, important for immunity and metabolism.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Whole grain pasta contains gluten, so individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should choose gluten‑free alternatives.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Cream sauce can be high in saturated fat; those monitoring cholesterol may opt for light cream or substitutes.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: When seasoning the sauce, keep salt levels moderate to avoid excessive sodium intake.

items.title: Cooking hazards
items.content: Handling hot sauce and boiling pasta requires care to prevent burns.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Cook whole grain pasta in salted water until al dente (usually 10‑12 minutes). In a skillet, sauté chicken pieces until golden, then add cream, a little flour, salt, pepper, and herbs; simmer until thickened. Toss the pasta with the sauce, heat together for 1‑2 minutes, and serve hot, garnished with fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared pasta in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. Cream sauce is best used within 24 hours. For longer storage, freeze individual portions up to 1 month after cooling and sealing in a freezer‑safe bag.
